title: Great concept but could use some refinements
body: I love the idea of being able to grow a garden by completing my habits, but the all or nothing aspect is so frustrating. If I miss only one out of 6 of my habits, nothing happens. Behaviourally this means people will say it’s not worth trying to do any of the habits for the day if they know they’re going to miss one. There should be proportional reward for taking partial action so that even completing 5/6 habits gets rewarded, but completing 6/6 gets rewarded more.

title: Two major faults for an otherwise great app
body:
I think Eden is a really beautiful app, and I especially love the widget to keep my habits front and centre. I do have two major complaints with it though. The first is that there is no way to move the order of habits around. So if you’re like me and write a list chronologically, and want to add something for midday, you have to manually delete and fill in every single subsequent habit. It’s frustrating.

 The second is that while this is the only app that I have felt motivated to stick to my habits, I find it equally discouraging that my plants do not grow if I don’t complete *every single* habit each day. For someone like me where it’s a huge accomplishment to finally achieve maybe 5/6 habits on a regular basis these days, I wish some parts of the plant still grew for the things I did accomplish, instead of punishing for the one that I didn’t. I paid for the premium version but I’m considering getting a refund for this alone. I just wish there was some acknowledgement of the things I have actually succeeded instead of the things that I fail.
